name: Killdozer
label: Touch and Go
lede: Three guys from Madison named themselves after a TV movie about a killer bulldozer, made Butch Vig's name before Nirvana did, covered American Pie at a crawl, and quit on a tour called Fuck You, We Quit!

eras.title: A killer bulldozer in Madison
eras.text: Michael Gerald and the Hobson brothers made slow, heavy, funny records about losers and small-town Americana, cut at Smart Studio in Madison with future members of Garbage. Touch and Go signed them early and kept them for thirteen years.

years.h: Killdozer forms in Madison, named for a TV movie
years.p: Singer and bassist Michael Gerald, guitarist Bill Hobson and his brother, drummer Dan Hobson, take their name from Killdozer!, a 1974 TV movie about a possessed bulldozer based on a Theodore Sturgeon story.

years.h: Intellectuals Are the Shoeshine Boys of the Ruling Elite
years.p: Killdozer's debut album on Touch and Go, joining a Midwest roster with [[Die Kreuzen|7550b236-f9c2-450c-81a6-fac63bf9d23e]], [[Butthole Surfers|2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8]], [[Scratch Acid|75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0]] and [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]].

years.h: Snakeboy, cut at Smart Studio with Butch Vig
years.p: Recorded in March 1985 at Smart Studio in Madison, produced by Steve Marker with [[Butch Vig|ba30915c-4d33-43c5-8c37-ead0b8061517]] and Duke Erikson recording and mixing. Fans still shout for King of Sex.
years.xp: Much of the album is about Michael Gerald's encounter with a man named Bill Reisman. The only song Killdozer didn't write is a cover of Neil Young's Cinnamon Girl. Jessica Noll plays violin on River.

eras.title: Burl Ives, Butch Vig and American Pie
eras.text: Killdozer never toured much, since everyone had day jobs, but the records kept coming. One of them made Butch Vig the producer Kurt Cobain and Billy Corgan wanted.

years.p: Killdozer's EP takes its name from the folk singer and actor Burl Ives.

years.h: Twelve Point Buck puts Butch Vig on Kurt Cobain's radar
years.p: According to Wikipedia, this Killdozer album brought producer Butch Vig to the attention of [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] and [[Billy Corgan|3cbfd3e3-6d9b-4327-84ba-42cf646c98f9]], two years before Nevermind and Gish.

years.h: For Ladies Only: Killdozer covers American Pie
years.p: An all-covers album: Don McLean's American Pie, Jessi Colter's I'm Not Lisa and the Trammps' Disco Inferno, all dragged through Killdozer's sludge.

years.h: Her Mother's Sorrow single on Amphetamine Reptile
years.p: Killdozer releases the 7" Her Mother's Sorrow, with Short Eyes on the B-side, on Minneapolis label Amphetamine Reptile.

eras.title: Marxist titles and an Albini album
eras.text: Bill Hobson left and Killdozer stopped. When it came back in 1993 with a new guitarist, it had a new target: the album titles turned into leftist slogans and the last studio record was cut with Steve Albini.

years.h: Bill Hobson leaves and Killdozer stops
years.p: Guitarist Bill Hobson leaves and Killdozer's first run ends.

years.h: Killdozer returns with guitarist Paul Zagoras
years.p: Michael Gerald and Dan Hobson restart Killdozer with Paul Zagoras on guitar and release the single The Pig Was Cool.

years.h: Uncompromising War on Art Under the Dictatorship of the Proletariat
years.p: The comeback album's title reads like a Communist Party pamphlet. The CD adds the whole Burl EP.

years.src: Wikipedia: God Hears Pleas of the Innocent
years.h: God Hears Pleas of the Innocent, recorded by Steve Albini
years.p: Killdozer's last studio album, cut in September 1994 at the House That Dripped Blood in Chicago with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. The only cover is Lee Hazlewood's Pour Man.
years.xp: The Washington Post heard an alternate universe where Black Sabbath taught Robert Johnson the blues. The Chicago Tribune called it uproariously brutish, heavy and slow.
play: God Hears Pleas of the Innocent

years.h: We Will Crush You, a split 10" with Ritual Device
years.p: Killdozer shares a 10" with Ritual Device on Man's Ruin Records.

years.h: Killdozer's farewell tour: Fuck You, We Quit!
years.p: Killdozer calls it a day with a tour officially titled Fuck You, We Quit!, adding Jeff Ditzenberger on second guitar.

eras.title: Fuck You, We Reunite!
eras.text: After the farewell, the members scattered into law, film crews and Madison bar bands. Touch and Go's 25th birthday brought the original trio back with the obvious slogan.

years.h: The Last Waltz, Killdozer live on the way out
years.p: Man's Ruin releases a live album from the farewell run, borrowing its title from the Band's famous goodbye. Crustacean reissues it in 2006.
Michael Gerald becomes a lawyer in Los Angeles and Bill Hobson a film grip there. Dan Hobson stays in Madison and plays in Cement Pond, whose Vanilla Guerilla comes out in 2005.

years.h: Original Killdozer reunites for Touch and Go's 25th
years.p: Michael Gerald and Bill and Dan Hobson play Touch and Go's anniversary weekend in Chicago, billed with the slogan Fuck You, We Reunite!

years.h: Touch and Go announces a Killdozer US tour
years.p: The reunited trio returns for American dates in fall 2008. Gerald also sings on a Hunchback cover for their album Pray for Scars.
